newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jiangxi Copper's Hong Kong IPO 33 times subscribed.
newsitem.headline: Jiangxi Copper's Hong Kong IPO 33 times subscribed.

text.p: China copper producer Jiangxi Copper Co Ltd said on Tuesday its offering of 62.822 million H-shares in Hong Kong was 32.9 times subscribed.
The Hong Kong initial public offering (IPO) represents 10 percent of the global offering.
The company said the price of the new issue had been fixed at HK$2.55 per share, with dealing in the H-shares expected to begin on June 12.
Jiangxi Copper offered 628.212 million H-shares at an indicative price ranging from HK$2.13 to HK$2.72. The shares will have a secondary listing on the London Stock Exchange.
Jiangxi Copper is engaged in copper mining, milling, smelting and refining in China's northeastern Jiangxi province.
The company said proceeds would be used to repay short-term debt, with the balance used to expand production facilities.

The company's parent Jiangxi Copper Co is controlled by China National Non-Ferrous Metals Corp, which was set up by the State Council to manage and hold a portion of the non-ferrous metals industry in China.
